They carry most of the aroma and are used where whole pods are not practical, for example in some spice blends, bakery recipes and beverage mixes. If you are not sure which form suits you, we are glad to talk it through. Many buyers who make coffee blends choose whole green cardamom instead, because the pod helps protect the aroma. Seeds or whole pods? Whole pods protect the seeds, so aroma lasts longer in storage, and size and colour are easy to check by eye. Seeds save the step of removing the husk, which suits blenders who want only the kernel. Because seeds lose fragrance faster once out of the pod, they are best bought in quantities you can use within a reasonable time. What is green cardamom? Green cardamom is a spice made from the small, oval seed pods of a plant in the ginger family. Inside each pod are tiny dark seeds that carry the aroma. It is often called the “queen of spices” because of its fragrance and value. It is the cardamom used in chai, Arabic coffee, kheer, biryani and many sweets. It is a different spice from black cardamom, which is larger and smoky. Read the differences between green and black cardamom . Where it grows Green cardamom needs warm, humid, shaded hill country with steady rain. In India the best-known growing areas are in the Western Ghats, including Idukki in Kerala. Quick answer: choose the grade by what you will use it for, not just by price. Larger grades look and smell better and cost more. Smaller grades work well when the cardamom will be ground or blended. AGEB Extra Bold Pods of about 8 mm and above, bright green and strongly aromatic. Best for premium retail, gifting and Arabic coffee, where the look of the pod matters. AGB Bold Pods of about 7.5 to 8 mm. A balanced everyday choice for chai, sweets and home use, with good colour and aroma at a lower price than AGEB. AGS Superior Pods of about 7 to 7.5 mm. For everyday chai and cooking, take AGB. For a restaurant kitchen or large blends, take AGS. For grinding into masala, small pods are enough.
